title: Embedding Robustness: Noise & Length Probe Suite
content:
Purpose:
This doc describes a targeted probe-suite for embedding sets intended to catch regressions that specific upstream changes (quantization, tokenization tweaks, batch-kernel swaps) can introduce in noisy or length-varied input distributions. Focus is multilingual (5 langs), and pragmatic search / clustering scenarios. The suite is designed for quick PR smoke runs (< 30s if cached) and a heavier nightly battery for regression detection.

Design goals:
- Cover realistic noise types engineers see in production search queries and user content: typos, punctuation stripping, emoji/code switching, url/email patterns, concatenated sentences, truncation.
- Measure sensitivity to input length extremes (very short 1–3 tokens; long 128–2048 tokens) and mid-range distributions observed in product telemetry.
- Multilingual parity checks: English, Spanish, Portuguese, Hindi, Japanese. Include script- and morphology-sensitive probes (e.g., tokenization boundary noise for Japanese/Hindi).
- Fast-to-run smoke tests + detailed regression metrics for nightly.
- Provide clear pass/fail thresholds and expected failure modes for triage.

Probe matrix (high level):
- Noise types: typo-insert (random character delete/insert), keyboard-substitution (q->w style), punctuation-strip, whitespace-collapse, emoji-insert, code-switch (insert 10–30% words from other language), url/email-masking (replace with token), repetition-attack (duplicate sentence), concatenation (2 distinct queries glued without separator).
- Length buckets: tiny (1–3 tokens), short (4–16), medium (17–128), long-seq (129–512), ultra-long (513–2048).
- Tasks: semantic-search (query→doc ranking), clustering (k-means purity), cross-lingual-retrieval (EN query → non-EN doc), neighbor-isotropy checks (nn distance distributions).

Datasets included in the suite:
- curated-qrels-5lang: 2k queries per language, relevance judgments derived from FAQ and support logs (de-identified).
- synthetic-noise-sweep: 400 canonical queries per lang x 8 noise types x lengths (constructed deterministically to be reproducible).
- multilingual-paraphrase-pairs: 3k pairs covering translation parity and paraphrase density (source: internal translation memory + CC-aligned subset).
- cluster-sanctum: 600 short documents per language arranged into 20 known clusters (topic-level), used for silhouette/purity checks.

Metrics collected:
- Retrieval: NDCG@10, MRR, Recall@100, mean reciprocal rank delta vs baseline.
- Clustering: Adjusted Rand Index (ARI), cluster purity, Silhouette score per-language and cross-language.
- Embedding diagnostics: pairwise cosine distribution (mean/std), nearest-neighbor language contamination rate (fraction of top-k neighbors from different language when they should be same), isotropy score (variance of singular values / top-eig ratio).
- Robustness deltas: relative change in metric vs pinned baseline model/version. We report absolute metric and percent change and flag regression when metric drops beyond threshold.

Pass/Fail thresholds (example):
- Smoke (quick PR): median cosine NN distance within +/- 6% of baseline; NDCG@10 drop < 3% absolute on curated-qrels-5lang; cluster purity drop < 5 percentage points.
- Nightly (heavy): NDCG@10 drop < 1.5% absolute; ARI drop < 0.03 absolute; isotropy change < 8% (unless model intentionally changed).
Notes: thresholds chosen to balance sensitivity to real regressions and avoid noisy false alarms; teams may tighten for canary/dedicated rollouts.

Implementation notes and reproducibility:
- All noise injectors are deterministic with fixed RNG seed and documented mutators in /eval/embedding-noise-mutators. Avoid non-deterministic augmentations in smoke runs.
- Use same tokenization pipeline as serving runtime for the eval (this catches tokenization drift). Test harness runs both raw-text pipeline and tokenized-stage embeddings to localize regressions (tokenizer vs encoder).
- For long-sequence embeddings, we provide two embedding-extraction modes: full-context chunking+pooling and sliding-window-last-k approach used by runtime. Tests run both to surface behavior differences.
- Cache precomputed document embeddings for nightly runs; smoke runs compute short queries-only live to catch embedding runtime regressions.

Regression triage playbook (when a check fails):
1) Re-run with --deterministic and --trace-logs to confirm.
2) Check tokenization diffs (tokenization output mismatch) between baseline and candidate for failing examples. If tokenization differs, open a tokenization/regression ticket and rollback tokenizer-related PRs.
3) If tokens match, compute per-layer mean activation deltas (if available) or per-position attention norm deltas to isolate model block causing drift.
4) Run iso test: pass identical inputs through baseline model quantized-mode vs candidate quantized-mode to see if quantization change is root cause.
5) If candidate is a new model checkpoint, compare embedding directionality (procrustes alignment) to determine if global rotation is occurring. If rotation exists but semantic ranking retained, we may accept with mapping for downstream index.

Reporting template (for nightly/regression report):
- summary_line: "NDCG@10 dropped 2.3% for es; top failing noise: punctuation-strip"
- failing_examples: list of 10 canonical examples with baseline vs candidate NN lists and scores
- diagnostics: tokenization_delta: yes/no; quantization_delta: yes/no; per-block-deltas: top3
- suggested_action: revert, tune-quant, investigate-tokenizer, accept-with-remap

Quick smoke command examples (developer):
- smoke (short): python eval/run_probe.py --suite noise_length_smoke --model candidate:latest --seed 42 --quick
- nightly (heavy): python eval/run_probe.py --suite noise_length_nightly --model candidate:latest --cache docs_cache --out report/$(date +%F)_candidate.json

Ownership and run cadence:
- eng-applied-ml owns the probe definitions and smoke runner.
- PR hook smoke: runs automatically on all embedding runtime and tokenizer PRs.
- Nightly battery: scheduled 02:00 UTC, artifacts stored for 90 days.
- On-call: eng-sre to monitor infra; applied-ml on-call to triage failing health.

Open questions / future improvements:
- Add real-world error distributions from telemetry (keyboard heatmap) per locale to weight noise injectors.
- Evaluate heavy code-switching (>50%) cases taken from social logs (privacy-preserved).
- Integrate a small learned adaptor step that maps new checkpoint embeddings to baseline space (auto-check acceptance criteria).

Appendix: small sample entries (canonical failing case format)
- id: es-noise-341
  input_clean: "¿Cómo reinicio mi cuenta?"
  input_noisy: "como reinicio mi cuenta" (punctuation-strip + lowercased)
  baseline_top1: "faq-reset-account" (score 0.78)
  candidate_top1: "faq-account-help" (score 0.69)
  delta_ndcg10: -0.045
  triage_flag: tokenization_delta=false, isotropy_drop=true

- id: jp-long-12
  input_clean: (Japanese long-form 520 tokens)
  failure_mode: neighbor-contamination (nearby English snippets surface in top5)
  suggested_action: run chunking+pooling vs sliding-window debug

If this doc looks good, next steps: convert canonical examples into a small dashboard in Redwood Console (embed-evals dashboard) and add automatic PR comment summaries for failing smoke tests.

Notes-to-self: keep smoke suite < 100 queries for quick feedback; nightly should include full 10k+ canonical set and preserve per-language telemetry splits.
